summary: Milestone 2026.04.112 completed 11 experiments in 40 minutes. The observed wall time was dominated by gate churn rather than productive GPU-bound work: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 reruns gated on the Exp 1414 repair executor consumed 25 minutes (62.5%), the legacy Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 gate consumed 10 minutes (25%), and a SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight doomed-rerun block consumed 2 minutes (5%). Both RTX 3090 GPUs were idle at closeout with no listed GPU processes or gpu_monitor.py zombie warnings. Estimated next-milestone savings are 55% if repeated same-verdict gates terminalize immediately, readiness artifacts are emitted at activation time, and independent model work uses DualGPURunner across both GPUs.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Repeated full-pipeline execution stayed gated on the repair-executor path instead of terminalizing once the upstream repair executor had no useful accepted-repair signal.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A known legacy arXiv bundle gate remained on the critical path instead of being represented by an activation-time terminal readiness artifact.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Duplicate same-verdict pipeline attempt on the Exp 1414 repair-executor dependency.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Additional repeated pipeline attempt with the same gate dependency and no evidence of new productive work.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Doomed-rerun block: SOTA GGUF Cache + Provenance Preflight - P
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Known cache/provenance readiness failure was rediscovered during execution instead of being emitted as a fast terminal preflight artifact.

bottlenecks_identified: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gate churn consumed 25 of 40 minutes (62.5%) across three slowest-five entries gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor.
The Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 legacy gate consumed 10 minutes (25%) and should not remain a recurring runtime discovery path.
The SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight still appears as a doomed-rerun execution slot instead of an immediate activation-time terminal artifact.
GPU utilization was inefficient for any LLM-bearing work: both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, each with only 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization.
No GPU zombie processes were observed: gpu_monitor.py reported an empty process list and no warnings, so the issue was idle capacity rather than leaked VRAM.
Independent Qwen/Gemma model checks and non-GPU documentation/reconciliation work were not visibly scheduled as parallel tracks in the supplied timing data.

The pre-flight suite was a secondary bottleneck rather than the dominant one; the supplied slowest-five data attributes only 2 minutes directly to preflight, but repeated known-blocked preflights still add avoidable churn.
Documentation reconciliation was not a top slowest-five item, but changelog and roadmap updates are recurring closeout work that should be handled by idempotent appenders.
improvements_suggested: Change full-pipeline gates to require nonzero accepted-repair or nonzero semantic-validation improvement before rerunning expensive pipeline validation.
Add same-verdict retirement for repeated Full-Scale Pipeline gate attempts so duplicate blocked/no-improvement verdicts terminalize after the first confirmed failure.
Emit activation-time terminal readiness artifacts for Exp 1269 arXiv bundle state and SOTA GGUF cache/provenance state instead of rediscovering known-blocked states during milestone execution.
Schedule independent LLM-bearing tasks with DualGPURunner: place Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 when both GPUs are free.
Record per-experiment GPU telemetry in result artifacts so retros can distinguish true CPU/doc work from missed GPU parallelism.
Shard and cache pre-flight checks by touched surface area; avoid blanket full-suite preflight for known-blocked or documentation-only slots.
Make docs reconciliation an idempotent closeout command that appends changelog and roadmap rows exactly once and reports no-op when rows already exist.
Add conductor timing categories for gate wait, preflight, GPU inference, docs, and artifact writing so future retros can attribute savings from structured data instead of slowest-five reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Terminalize repeated Full-Scale Pipeline v3 same-verdict gates and require nonzero repair/pipeline improvement before rerun.
Move Exp 1269 arXiv and SOTA GGUF cache/provenance readiness checks to activation-time terminal artifacts.
Use DualGPURunner plus per-experiment GPU telemetry for all independent Qwen/Gemma validation work.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor was the longest path: 14, 6, and 5 minute entries for 25 minutes total, caused by repeated same-dependency gate churn. arXiv Bundle v10 gated on Exp 1269 consumed another 10 minutes as a recurring legacy gate. SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight consumed 2 minutes rediscovering a known doomed-rerun state.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. The supplied and live gpu_monitor.py snapshots show both RTX 3090s idle with 4 MB allocated, 0% utilization, and no compute processes. Independent Qwen/Gemma tasks should be run concurrently across GPU 0 and GPU 1 when available.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No GPU zombie evidence was observed. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings; the 4 MB allocations appear to be trivial driver/context residue, not material VRAM leaks.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. Independent model readiness/smoke checks could run on separate GPUs, and docs/reconciliation work could run independently from non-overlapping preflight classification. Repeated blocked full-pipeline gates should mostly be retired rather than parallelized.
questions_answered.was_the_preflight_test_suite_a_bottlenec: Only secondarily in the supplied data. The direct slowest-five preflight cost was 2 minutes, far below the 25 minute pipeline gate churn and 10 minute arXiv gate. The preflight process is still inefficient when it rediscovers known-blocked states during execution.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Not a leading timing bottleneck in the provided slice, but recurring changelog/roadmap edits should be automated through idempotent appenders to avoid repeated manual closeout passes.
questions_answered.what_tooling_would_speed_next_milestone: Nonzero-success gates, same-verdict retirement, activation-time terminal readiness artifacts, DualGPURunner scheduling, per-experiment GPU telemetry, sharded/cached preflight, and idempotent ops-doc appenders.

meta_reflection: This retro reinforces that the milestone was already short in absolute time, but most remaining delay is structural and recurring. The next speedup should not come from asking agents to work faster; it should come from making known-blocked states terminal at activation, preventing same-verdict gate churn, and using the already-available dual-GPU capacity when live model work is actually runnable.
